title: Shared Bills and Personal Subscriptions for Couples
metaDescription: Split joint bills from personal subscriptions, spot the same service paid for twice and keep one list each. A manual tracker with no joint bank login.
h1: How can couples in India separate shared bills from personal subscriptions?
summary: Couples in India often pay for the same service twice without noticing: two music plans, two cloud storage plans, or two streaming logins, alongside rent, electricity and broadband that are split in some way. A manual tracker such as Essara helps each partner record their own subscriptions and their share of joint bills, see upcoming renewals, and spot overlaps, without connecting a bank account.
stepsHeading: Set up two lists with one agreed split

sections.heading: Shared bills versus personal subscriptions
paragraphs: Most arguments about money in a couple come from not knowing what is shared. Rent, electricity and broadband are usually joint, while a music plan, a gaming subscription or a fitness app is often personal. The problem is that personal subscriptions can quietly overlap: both partners may pay for storage, music or a streaming service that the other already has.

Decide the rule before you start. Either one partner keeps a joint list and both of you record only your share, or each of you keeps a personal list and the joint bills go on one of them. Essara's features are per account and do not include a joint or shared account, so the couple agrees the split in advance and each person records what they pay.

sections.heading: Deciding which of you keeps the shared plan
paragraphs: Duplicates usually show up in cloud storage, because each partner's phone asks for more space. Google One and Apple Family Sharing both let one person share a plan with others, and the plan rules are covered in the families guide, so the question here is simpler: which of you keeps the plan, and does the other stop paying for their own?

Check which plan you are on before you consolidate. Google's help page says sharing is not available on the 30 GB Lite plan, and Apple's Family Sharing gives up to five family members access to services such as iCloud+ and Apple Music without sharing one Apple Account.

sections.heading: When the plan sits under your partner's account
paragraphs: Cancelling is where couples most often get stuck, because the subscription may sit under the other partner's account. On Android, the subscription list only shows the Google Account you are signed into, so if you cannot find a plan, you may need to switch accounts. On iPhone, Apple says that if your partner's Apple Account is on the receipt, only they can cancel it, so ask them rather than trying yourself.
Google Play keeps access running until the end of the period already paid for. Agree in advance who cancels what, so neither of you finds out about a renewal from a bank message.

sections.heading: Joint UPI AutoPay mandates
paragraphs: A UPI AutoPay mandate is usually visible only in the UPI app of the person who approved it. If your partner set up a broadband or insurance mandate on their phone, you will not see it in yours. Ask them to write down the merchant, amount, frequency and next debit date, then enter it in your shared list under their name.
Pausing or cancelling a mandate needs the UPI PIN of the app that holds it, so agree in advance who manages each joint mandate.

sections.heading: Tracking both of you in Essara
paragraphs: Each partner can enter their own subscriptions and mandates, and the joint bills can be entered at each person's share, with the full amount in the entry name. The app then shows the monthly and yearly cost, the renewals for the next 30 days with a reminder before each one, and a monthly budget with a daily spending limit. It does not read bank, UPI or SMS data, so the list is only as accurate as what each of you enters.

steps.name: Agree on the split
steps.text: Decide which bills are joint, which subscriptions are personal, and who manages each joint bill.

steps.name: Each partner lists personal plans
steps.text: Open your Google Play or Apple subscriptions and the Autopay section of your UPI app, and note each item with its price and renewal date.

steps.name: Look for overlaps
steps.text: Compare the two lists side by side. Storage, music and streaming are the usual duplicates. Check whether one of you could join the other's plan.

steps.name: Create your accounts
steps.text: Each partner signs up at essara.space/signup or installs the Android app from Google Play. Each account works on Android and the web app.

steps.name: Add joint bills at your share
steps.text: Enter rent, electricity, broadband or phone at what you pay, with the full bill amount written in the entry name.

steps.name: Add personal subscriptions and mandates
steps.text: Enter each subscription with its cycle and renewal date, and each UPI AutoPay mandate on the account of the partner whose app holds it.

steps.name: Check reminders and the budget
steps.text: Check the 30-day renewals timeline, confirm a reminder is set before each renewal, then set a monthly budget with a daily spending limit.

faqs.q: Can my partner and I see one shared Essara list?
faqs.a: Not as a joint account. Essara's listed features do not include shared or joint accounts. Each of you keeps your own account, records your own subscriptions, and records your share of the joint bills. Agree the totals between you.

faqs.q: How do we stop paying for two storage plans?
faqs.a: Check whether one of you can join the other's Google One family group or Apple Family Sharing group. Google requires the manager to be 18 or older and invitees to live in the same country. Confirm the current rules on your plan before you cancel either one.

faqs.q: Can I cancel my partner's Apple subscription for them?
faqs.a: Not if it is their Apple Account on the receipt. Apple says only the Apple Account shown on the receipt can cancel it, so ask your partner to sign in and cancel it themselves.

faqs.q: Does Essara connect to our bank accounts?
faqs.a: No. Essara is manual. You add subscriptions, bills and UPI AutoPay mandates yourself. It never connects to your bank or UPI app, never reads SMS and never asks for your UPI PIN.
